program: XMRig 6.26.0, statically linked stripped Linux mining executables
verdict_basis: BENIGN for each standalone executable: recovered behavior matches its stated mining purpose; no concrete hostile behavior found. Mining capability and reputation do not prove unauthorized use.
limits: Static reverse engineering; samples were not executed.
Tagged upstream source comparison does not establish reproducible-build byte identity.
Surrounding deployment scripts, pool settings and operator authorization were not supplied.
The three supplied Triage pages could not be retrieved. No conclusions were drawn from their scores.
observations: Entrypoints perform static-PIE relocation and C runtime setup, then construct Process(argc, argv), handle help/version entry modes, construct App and call App::exec.
All three App::exec implementations test controller readiness before starting mining. Failure logs the configuration-wizard message and returns 2.

AArch64 config constructor 0x53160 tries transformed command-line input, data/config.json, home/.xmrig.json and home/.config/xmrig.json. On failure the resulting config pointer is null; no embedded pool/wallet fallback appears in this path.
Background fork/setsid is conditional on the configured background flag in all three implementations, with error handling. This is optional daemonization, not installation or persistence.
AArch64 Stratum client at 0x63fa0 constructs login parameters and the login RPC; 0x64dd0 constructs a submit request (call at 0x6526c). The work/result flow is mining, not shell-command tasking.

AArch64 donation constructor 0xe0b80 reads donateLevel, computes donation milliseconds as level*60000 and idle milliseconds as (100-level)*60000, and builds the upstream donate.v2.xmrig.com:3333 pool. No substituted donation destination found.
CryptoNight/RandomX/Argon2 hashing, CPU enumeration, hugepage settings and worker threads are consistent with a CPU miner. Scheme strings alone do not establish TLS operations.
All three ELF DT_NEEDED lists are empty. Embedded libuv version 1.51.0 and musl-style syscall implementations explain general networking and process helpers without implying a downloader dependency.
AArch64 connect wrapper 0x1f4b40 passes syscall 203 through 0x1fedc0 to 0x1fed9c, which copies x0 to x8, shifts arguments and executes SVC. sendto/recvfrom use the same helper with 206/207.
ARM socket wrapper at 0x217fa4 loads r7 from 0x21803c via LDR at 0x217fb0; that literal is 281. SVC at 0x217fbc creates the socket and subsequent branches handle CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK fallback.

i386 socket wrapper uses syscall 359 and a syscall-102 fallback with selector 1, EDX/EBX exchange and GS:[0x10] dispatch. bind fallback uses selector 2; connect prepares selector 3 and syscall 102 for its shared helper.
Original i386 findings at 0x30492, 0x31ab3 and 0x32dc5 were generic small-integer pushes into a C++ exception helper at 0x8d99. They were not socket operations.

Decoded-string facts were inspected for all samples. XOR candidates mostly transform already-readable algorithm names, CPU names, format errors and code bytes; the URL-decoded date format and Base64 candidates do not yield a payload. No intentional encoded malicious layer was recovered.
No recovered path established credential theft, persistence installation, exploitation, victim file encryption, rival-process killing, hidden payload retrieval or unauthorized resource use.
external_label_explanation: Generic Linux CoinMiner/XMRig/Application/PUA labels recognize a real miner. A miner can also be collected as the payload of a hostile deployment without carrying that deployment behavior in its standalone executable.
trait_changes: Replace the three generic i386 push/call atoms with socketcall-specific register/argument/dispatch sequences in socket/create, bind/function and connect. Update the existing network composite.
Move the AArch64 socket wrapper to socket/create and constrain it to .text. Update both exact consumers.
Move the ARM literal-pool socket wrapper to socket/create, retain both old pool-distance variants, and add the verified 0x84 LDR variant. Update exact consumers.

Move three ARM ELF architecture facts from metadata/arch/iot to metadata/arch/arm with identical matchers and scope. Update exact consumers, the embedded-architecture grouping and the architecture directory exclusion.
Move Stratum URL schemes to communications/url/scheme, preserving matchers, scopes and exclusions. Rewrite exact and same-leaf consumers; a URL reference is not a socket operation.

Replace XMRig lowercase name-only identity with a composite requiring the product reference plus path-variable and donation-banner fingerprints. Product references retain their process/info/name finding. Retire the former identity-specific suppressors because the stronger identity describes XMRig implementations, including forks, rather than declaring them malicious.
Add a notable JSON-RPC keepalived request-body trait; it establishes a request template, not a C2 beacon.

Audit the full socket/connect leaf at its 100-rule budget. Consolidate identical socket_connect call matchers from C/C++ and PHP into one canonical atom (scope union, also admitting C/C++ on Windows). Update consumers and keep the PHP dial grouping explicitly PHP-scoped. The other call sites retain their existing language scopes.

coverage: ARM PC-relative pool binding and architecture
